_note: Provider registration — inner extensibility without a second kernel (local-ai-engine.md §4.11). THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) a provider is a MODULE (a child under `Core/LocalAI/Modules/`, or any module including a per-app Custom one) that declares `facets.provider` rows: a modality id, the action that serves it, the backend it needs. (2) The registry is derived from those rows at build time — nothing downloads code, nothing registers dynamically at runtime (the dynamic-split law). (3) A provider whose backend this build does not carry is INERT and answers typed absence; it never shadows a working one. (4) Two enabled modules claiming the same modality id is a BUILD abort, not a runtime coin-flip — the same enabled-claimant collision rule the facet grammar already enforces. (5) A per-app provider is a full citizen: it plugs into the same loop, the same streaming envelope, the same approval flow, and the same fit and routing — 'add an output nobody has built' means exactly this and nothing more magical. (6) The residency law holds: parent actions stay on `intelligence`, and a child adds NEW actions on its own chain.

cases.name: provider: a declared row serves its modality through the container
cases._note: The voice child declares it serves the `speech` modality with `synthesize`, backed by the `tts` engine. A call to the child chain reaches it and streams; the parent scheme keeps its own actions untouched.

cases.name: provider: a per-app module registers a modality nobody shipped
cases._note: The extensibility promise, executed. A Custom module declares a `music` modality served by its own action over its own backend; it appears in the registry, streams through the same envelope, and is routable — with zero kernel changes and zero changes to the AI package.

cases.name: provider: a provider whose backend is missing is inert and typed
cases._note: The row is declared but this build carries no such backend — the provider registers as unavailable with the reason, and the call answers typed absence. It must NOT shadow anything or pretend to serve.

cases.name: provider: two enabled claimants of one modality abort the build
cases._note: The collision guard, at the layer where it belongs. This is a PREPARE-time abort (the enabled-claimant key collision the facet grammar already enforces), never a runtime last-writer-wins — a per-app module colliding with a framework child must fail loudly at build time.

cases.name: provider: an excluded claimant frees the modality for the other
cases._note: The other half of the collision rule: exclusion is the resolution. With the framework child excluded, the per-app provider claims `speech` cleanly — which is exactly how an app replaces a built-in modality with its own.
